text: Since a seizure is one of the main dangers while you wait, I'd use [DMSO](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/170920118/dmso), which seems to help prevent them, going by people's reports rather than studies: at any sign of an overdose, have them smell it or rub a little on a clean patch of skin (with 30% water if the skin itches), then use a little more at a time, since some people react more strongly than others. You might also think of [niacin](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/170920118/niacin-flushes-trips-out), which this guide uses for ending a trip, but it's unsafe with serotonin syndrome, since at that dose it can cause flushing and a drop in blood pressure ([NIH](https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Niacin-Consumer/)). The other remedy I'd keep for a last resort, if nothing else is helping and no medics are coming, is [Syrian rue oil](https://ibogaqueen.substack.com/i/170920118/syrian-rue-oil-gentler), since it makes trips, ayahuasca included, much less intense. The oil isn't the Syrian rue brew from step 1, which blocks MAO and is dangerous with MDMA for that reason, but nobody has studied the oil with MDMA either.
reader: a friend sitting with someone who took MDMA on top of their antidepressant and now has twitching muscles, sweating and a racing heart; they have called an ambulance and read what to do while they wait

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here?
